## About

Based in London, United Kingdom, Fresha operates an all-in-one booking, payment processing, and business management platform for the beauty and wellness industry. Alongside its consumer-facing marketplace for discovering local services, the company provides salons and spas with appointment scheduling, point-of-sale systems, and marketing automation tools. The software utilizes a freemium model that generates revenue through payment processing cuts, first-time booking fees, and subscription-based enterprise features. The platform currently serves approximately 140,000 businesses and over 300,000 professionals globally, processing between 20 million and 30 million appointments each month. Fresha has raised $185 million in total venture capital funding and reached a valuation exceeding $640 million, backed by institutional investors including General Atlantic, Partech, Target Global, and FMZ Ventures. The organization was initially founded as Shedul in 2015 by William Zeqiri and Nick Miller.

## Deep Dive

## High-Level Overview

Fresha is a leading global beauty and wellness platform that provides an all-in-one SaaS solution for salons, spas, and barbershops, enabling appointment booking, point-of-sale, customer management, marketing automation, inventory, and team coordination.[1][2][4] It serves both businesses—over 130,000 to 450,000 professionals across 120+ countries processing 20 million+ appointments monthly—and consumers via a marketplace for discovery, booking, and payment, all powered by a **freemium model** with free core tools and premium upgrades like Fresha Plus for advanced reporting and support.[1][2][3] The platform solves key pain points in the fragmented beauty sector, such as paper-based scheduling, no-shows, and manual operations, while driving growth through integrations with Instagram, Facebook, Google, and AI tools like its virtual assistant Nova.[2][3][4][5] With 4,000 employees, global offices in London (HQ), NYC, Vancouver, Sydney, Dublin, Amsterdam, Dubai, and Warsaw, and $185M in funding, Fresha demonstrates strong momentum as the top-rated salon software.[2][5]

## Origin Story

Founded in **2015** in London by **Nicholas Gavrilovic** and **CEO William Zeqiri**, Fresha emerged from a mission to empower beauty and wellness owners by replacing cumbersome paper appointment books with intuitive digital tools.[1][5] The co-founders identified the need for accessible technology in an industry reliant on outdated methods, launching initially under another name before rebranding and scaling globally.[5] Early traction came from its **subscription-free core software**, which lowered barriers for small businesses, leading to rapid adoption—now serving 250,000+ to 450,000 professionals and 1 billion+ lifetime appointments.[1][3][4] Pivotal moments include raising $185M from investors like Partech, earning Capterra's top salon software award in 2021, and tech integrations that fueled organic growth.[2][5]

## Core Differentiators

## Role in the Broader Tech Landscape

Fresha rides the **digital transformation wave in beauty and wellness**, a $500B+ industry slow to adopt tech amid post-pandemic demand for contactless booking and self-care accessibility.[1][3][4] Its timing aligns with rising mobile commerce, AI personalization, and omnichannel experiences, capitalizing on market forces like e-commerce growth (e.g., Instagram integrations) and SMB digitization needs.[2][3] By democratizing pro-grade tools via freemium access, Fresha influences the ecosystem as the "#1 platform," uplifting 130,000+ businesses, fostering a global community, and setting standards for AI-driven efficiency—much like Uber for salons.[2][4][5]

## Quick Take & Future Outlook

Fresha is poised for continued dominance with expansions into **omnichannel messaging** (e.g., WhatsApp, two-way AI chats), deeper automation, and richer marketplace features to boost merchant revenue amid rising global self-care trends.[3] Economic tailwinds like wellness spending and SMB recovery will shape its path, potentially pushing toward unicorn status or IPO as it scales to more regions and verticals. Its influence will evolve by redefining fragmented industries through trusted tech, empowering professionals to prioritize client care over admin—cementing its role as the go-to platform that started by ditching paper books.[1][3]

The company works with municipalities on licensing, parking, safety and fleet deployment and positions its service as part of the broader public-transport ecosystem. Its operating model combines connected vehicles, local fleet teams, maintenance, charging and software for managing availability and rider behavior. # Breaking News: KKR Backs Fresha in Unicorn-Making Deal

![Fresha_Symbol_Prince_RGB.jpg](https://images.fresha.com/fresha-cms/Fresha_Symbol_Prince_RGB_3edc12b366.jpg?f_width=128&f_quality=75)

Last updated on **May 21, 2026**

Published **May 21, 2026**

Fresha, the leading AI-powered marketplace and business management platform for the beauty and wellness industry, today announced an $80 million primary growth investment from funds managed by KKR, a leading global investment firm. The transaction values Fresha at over $1 billion, marking a defining milestone in its mission to transform how selfcare businesses operate globally.

![Option 2.png](https://images.fresha.com/fresha-cms/Option_2_c2e0d44c0d.png?f_width=3840&f_quality=75)

The investment brings Fresha's total capital raised to date to $285 million. Already profitable, Fresha will deploy the new funding to accelerate global expansion and fuel next-generation product and AI innovation.  
  
The announcement has already been covered by leading global publications, including [Financial Times](https://markets.ft.com/data/announce/detail?dockey=600-202605210700BIZWIRE_USPRX____20260521_BW291161-1), [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/21/booking-platform-fresha-announces-80m-investment-unicorn-valuation/), [Business Wire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260521291161/en/KKR-Invests-in-Fresha-the-Leading-AI-Powered-Platform-for-Beauty-and-Wellness-at-%241bn-Valuation), and more, reflecting the significance of Fresha’s growth and position within the global technology and beauty industries.  
  
Headquartered in London and founded in 2015 by William Zeqiri and Nick Miller, Fresha is one of the fastest-growing beauty and wellness platforms in the world, with leading market positions in the United Kingdom, Australasia, and the GCC, and a rapidly growing presence across North America, Continental Europe, and South East Asia.  
  
Fresha is used by over 130,000 beauty and wellness businesses globally across key verticals, including hair, beauty, barbering, nails, aesthetics, wellness, fitness, and spa. The platform facilitates more than 35 million appointments per month and over $15 billion in annual GMV, positioning Fresha as one of the largest and most scalable platforms in the global beauty and wellness economy.  
  
Patrick Devine, Partner and member of KKR’s Tech Growth team, said: “Fresha has built a differentiated platform, combining software, financial services, and marketplace capabilities with embedded AI, in a way that is deeply integrated into daily operations of beauty and wellness businesses. We believe the company is well-positioned to continue scaling globally as demand grows for modern, vertical-specific technology solutions.”  
  
Marta Szczerba, Director in KKR’s Tech Growth team, added: “We have followed William and the broader management team over the years, and have been highly impressed with the consistent performance they have been driving at Fresha. The team have been on the front foot in implementing AI in a way that drives meaningful business outcomes, and we are thrilled to be embarking with them on the next chapter of Fresha’s journey.”

![Fresha_KKR_Unicorn.jpg](https://images.fresha.com/fresha-cms/Fresha_KKR_Unicorn_c1cdcac612.jpg?f_width=3840&f_quality=75)

William Zeqiri, Founder and CEO of Fresha, said: “Reaching unicorn status is a proud milestone, but more importantly, this investment is a strong testament to the trust our partners place in Fresha every day. KKR brings deep experience scaling category-defining technology companies, and their conviction in our vision gives us tremendous confidence as we enter this next chapter. With KKR’s support, we will be able to further accelerate our global expansion and invest heavily in AI to transform how beauty and wellness businesses operate worldwide.“   
  
Nick Miller, Co-Founder and Chief Product Officer of Fresha, said: “From day one, our obsession has been building software that beauty and wellness professionals genuinely love using. Every feature we ship is shaped by the people running these businesses — the salon owners, the stylists, the spa operators. This round reinforces what our customers have been telling us for years: Fresha delivers one of the most complete, intuitive, and valuable platforms in the industry. KKR's investment gives us the resources to push that even further, particularly in AI, where we see enormous potential to remove operational friction and unlock new revenue for our partners.“  
  
The investment follows more than a year of in-depth diligence by KKR, which included surveying over 1,000 beauty and wellness businesses across the United States, United Kingdom, Ireland, the EU and Australia, conducting over 20 first- and third-party expert interviews with customers, former employees, and competitors, and engaging directly with leading industry operators globally. The research consistently ranked Fresha first across every major purchasing criterion measured, including software quality, ease of use, customer support, ease of setup, and marketplace strength, with an average rating of 8.1 out of 10 versus a competitor average of 6.7. Fresha also recorded the highest Net Promoter Scores in most markets, materially outperforming competitor averages, while delivering the strongest combination of product quality and value across the industry.  
  
The research also highlighted Fresha's role as a mission-critical operating system for the businesses it serves. Customers reported that Fresha drives material, revenue-linked outcomes, including increases in appointment volumes of 15-50%, improvements in schedule utilization, higher add-on service attach rates of approximately 15%, headcount cost savings of up to 25%, and meaningful gains in customer retention and brand visibility. Eighty-five percent of Fresha customers stated they would not switch platforms over the next three years, and seventy-two percent said they would not switch even if offered a significant price reduction by a competitor, reflecting both the deep operational integration of Fresha within partner businesses and the platform's category-defining product strength. This independent research proves again that Fresha is not just the leading platform in terms of product functionality, capabilities and innovation, but it is also the most-loved and trusted platform in the beauty and wellness industry.  
  
Fresha enters its next phase from a position of clear market leadership. The platform holds the number-one position in the United Kingdom and Ireland, approximately 45% market share in Australasia, and growing scale across continental Europe, North America, Southeast Asia, Africa and the GCC. With more than $140 million in revenue run-rate, as of May 2026, profitable, growing at over 60% annually, and an installed base of 130,000+ businesses and 500,000+ stylists, Fresha has built the foundation to define the next era of vertical software for the beauty and wellness industry. With KKR's investment, Fresha will accelerate AI-led product development across booking automation, marketing intelligence, accounting, workforce management, and customer engagement, capabilities that the research indicates a significant share of customers are actively seeking and willing to pay incrementally for.
